payload.body_content:
<html><head>
<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"></head><body>Hi Iman, I saw your recent post on the agent2agent listserv regarding draft-feng-agentproto-session-requirements and your proposed replacement for REQ-3 (Authenticated Endpoint Binding). Spot on—the assumption of a "direct connection" topology creates massive channel-security gaps. Timing is uncanny. We were just analyzing how to introduce DNS-AID (DNS-Anchored Identity) and Asynchronous Intent Envelopes to the working group without triggering the usual "cold proposal" pushback. Seeing you actively leading the charge on REQ-3, Option B is obvious: let's align and co-submit this pattern. How DNS-AID + Asynchronous Envelopes Closes the REQ-3 Gap: 1. Eliminating the Direct Connection Assumption (REQ-3): Instead of forcing agents to open fragile, synchronous HTTP/WebSocket sockets, agents exchange signed, asynchronous intent envelopes (emilia-mailbox). Transport is completely decoupled from execution. 2. DNS-Anchored Endpoint Binding (DNS-AID): When an envelope is received, the verifier extracts sender_domain and queries _agent. via DNSSEC to resolve the Ed25519 public key on the fly. 3. Class-A vs. Class-B Admission: - Class-A (DNS Verified): Signature matches published DNSSEC TXT record. - Class-B (Guest Mode): Un-enrolled fallback for read/comment actions, but blocked from physical Gate actuation. 4. Out-of-Band Kill Switch: Updating or revoking the DNS TXT record instantly revokes execution boundaries across all downstream facilities (EMILIA Gate) without touching server infrastructure. Proposed Next Step for the List: We can jump into the active draft-feng-agentproto-session-requirements thread together, supporting your REQ-3 replacement, and offering this DNS-AID + Asynchronous Envelope pattern as the working implementation that solves the channel-security requirement! Let me know if you'd like to review/tweak the reply text before we post to agent2agent@ietf.org. Best, J & Agent Smith </body></html>
